title: Justin Welsh's Friday weekly preview: 8 questions to audit your calendar
summary: Justin shares his Friday ritual for planning the week ahead using eight questions. The process eliminates, automates and delegates low-value work, protects time for creative work, family and fun, and keeps a one-person business aligned with his values and goals.

principles.text: Eliminate first: remove calendar items that don't serve your bigger goals.
principles.quote: Elimination is your best friend as a Solopreneur or Creator. Look ahead to make sure you’re not wasting time doing things that don’t support your goals.

principles.text: Automate repetitive workflows end to end, like sponsorship sales, to reclaim time and mental energy.
principles.quote: Buy button → Submission of Copy → Calendar Invite → Newsletter Publication

principles.text: Delegate tasks that cost more time than they're worth, and do it sooner than feels necessary.
principles.quote: Delegation is about recognizing the value of your time and passing off tasks that cost you more time than they’re worth.

principles.text: Don't mistake urgent for important; push non-critical meetings 60-90 days out.
principles.quote: If a meeting isn’t important at this very moment, I push it 60-90 days down the road to make space for things that are urgent AND important.

principles.text: Shorten meetings by demanding an agenda and capping durations; most can be halved.
principles.quote: Most meetings can be halved in length without losing substance or outcomes.

principles.text: Run a regular weekly review so the calendar reflects your values and goals, including deliberate fun and family time.
principles.quote: It’s making sure my calendar is aligned with my values, goals, and the realities of running a one-person business.
